Create a finished For Garden in-game BATTLEFIELD concept replacing the discarded cute common battlefields. Precisely match the original game's thin hand-drawn dark violet contours, flat matte cel-painted shadows, restrained hand-painted gouache surface variation, simplified anime background illustration and believable chipped materials. Reference 1 is the original battle asset: reproduce its portrait camera, floor perspective and playable-space balance. Reference 2 is the ancient fossil-strata underground shaft map: new battlefield must feel like a room inside THAT location, sharing dusty lavender-gray rock, blue-violet shadows, old fossils, worn stone, restrained warm amber lanterns. Reference 3 shows the fossil sediment material language; adapt its earthy brown/ochre layers in small accents. The result must read unmistakably as an enclosed underground MINE TUNNEL battle arena, mostly natural stratified rock plus practical aged pit supports, not a courtyard, museum, laboratory room, garden, toy world, cake dungeon or sci-fi station. NO sky, sunlight from open outdoors, pastries, bunting, mascot banners, cute faces, paw symbols, white circle-and-cross symbol, people, characters, UI, numbers, text, logo or watermark. No photorealism, glossy rendering, 3D or neon. EXACT OUTPUT 941 pixels wide and 1672 pixels high, exact ratio 941:1672 matching the original 1882x3344 battlefield. Carefully avoid a one-pixel-short result. Ground-level slightly elevated camera with a broad flat floor filling lower TWO THIRDS, clear staging space for fighters. Environment detail and all obstacles concentrated at upper third and outer edges; tiny sparse floor cracks and stones only. Do not put a deep shaft, pit, central rail, large rock or prop through playable floor. Full bleed ONE portrait scene.An abandoned ancient-strata mine haulage junction: stratified violet-gray rock walls and low curved rock ceiling, old heavy timber pit props with corroded steel brackets framing left and right, a mine-cart siding and tiny parked ore cart confined to the far right side, a dark supported tunnel opening at upper center-left, hanging simple warm amber oil-like work lamps. Fossil ammonite impressions and a few exposed bone fragments embedded in layered rock at rear. Main floor is broad flat compacted pale dusty sediment and worn cracked stone, no rail crossing the center.
